idiom_name: static factory methods over a private constructor (static from/of) plus module-level factory functions
implementation_notes: TypeScript keeps the JavaScript mechanism and adds the type-system half: a private constructor is actually enforced by the compiler, a static from(input: unknown): T gives the validating route a name, and the declared return type can be an interface so implementation classes stay invisible while static members carry the same visibility modifiers as instance members. Generic static factories also solve the inference problem constructors have (of<T>(value: T): Box<T> infers T), and module-level factory functions remain the right shape when the class should not be exported at all; the pattern's classic structure is replaced by private-constructor plus static members, not by a separate factory class.
pitfalls: private constructor is compile-time only: the emitted JavaScript still allows new Email(...) or a cast through any, so runtime invariants must also be validated inside the constructor.
A static factory with a union parameter (from(value: string | number)) recreates constructor overload ambiguity; keep one factory per input shape so the type checker can narrow.

Returning an interface from a static factory erases the concrete class for downstream callers and for structural typing (private fields make classes nominally incompatible); return the class type or a branded type when identity matters.
